verdict.reasoning: Patient says: "I have had a pain in my lower tummy the last two days. I feel kind of hot and sweaty."
Doctor asks: "Is it in the middle or to one side?" Patient replies: "... it's my lower tummy." and clarifies "In the middle, OK." indicating midline lower abdominal pain.
Patient states: "Uh, no. I'm just a bit nausea but no vomiting." and later repeats "just a bit of nausea but not vomiting."

Patient reports: "I had been constipated in, like, in the last, um, last week, but now it's fine" and when asked "When did you last go to the toilet?" replies "like two hours ago" and confirms "Yeah" that it was normal.

Patient notes: "there was some, like, slight, uh, blood in the urine, but, like, it was a little bit pink" and "Are you having to go more often than normal?" – "uh, yeah, a little bit"; "Any pain when you pass water?" – "uh, no, that's fine"; "Are you more thirsty than normal?" – "uh, yeah"; "any, any back pain" – "Uh, no back pain."
Patient says: "I measured it but it's fine, like, around thirty seven" and when asked if measured at any other time answers: "Um, no, no, I just measured, like, one hour ago."

Doctor asks: "are you getting any pain higher up in your stomach? Any acid coming up into your throat or anything like that?" Patient responds: "No, no, but like just a bit of nausea but not vomiting."
Doctor asks: "And any other discharge below?" Patient replies: "Uh, no."
Doctor asks: "have you been abroad recently?" – "Um, no, no." and "And no similar problems to this before?" – Patient: "No."
When asked about other medical problems, patient says: "Um, no, no, nothing sore. I mean, depends what, like, normal stuff like cold, flu." Doctor summarizes: "OK, nothing significant."
Doctor: "Do you take any regular medications?" Patient: "Uh, no." Doctor: "Any over the counter medications?" Patient: "No."
Doctor asks about allergies; patient replies: "Uh, yes, amoxycillin."

Living: Doctor: "Who do you live with at home?" Patient: "Uh, with my parents." Smoking/alcohol: Doctor: "do you smoke or drink alcohol regularly?" Patient: "Uh, yes." then clarifies "so, I don't smoke. I drink... Four times per week." and "let's say a beer... Four times a week on average."
Patient states: "actually my mom had the breast cancer... it was , uh, cured in time."

Doctor assessment: "it may be possible that you might be having an infection in the urine" and recommends antibiotics. This fits suspected uncomplicated UTI given 2 days of midline lower tummy pain, pink urine, slight increased frequency, sweats, normal temperature, and explicitly "no back pain" and "no" pain when passing water.
Doctor: "it might be worth taking a three day course of antibiotics" and later: "Start taking them as soon as you get them, it's just twice a day for three days."

Doctor advises: "if the pain is getting worse, or you have a high temperature or back pain or develop any new symptoms, we feel like it's not getting better, then, um, we should speak to you again, because we might need to see you face-to-face for an examination."
Doctor adds: "or if you're getting a recurrence of the same problem again." and "just contact us straightaway" indicating re-contact for recurrence.
